summaryBox.title: Quick Section Summary
summaryBox.takeaway: Pedigree analysis tracks transmission of genetic traits across successive generations using standardized symbols. Three major modes: (1) Autosomal Dominant: does NOT skip generations; affected child MUST have an affected parent; (2) Autosomal Recessive: skips generations; unaffected carrier parents (Aa × Aa) yield affected children (aa); (3) X-Linked Recessive: predominantly affects males (XdY); carrier mother passes to 50% of sons; affected father passes to 100% of daughters (carriers).

conceptBreakdown.codeSnippet:
PEDIGREE SYMBOLS
                         
   Square       ──► Normal Male               Filled Square  ──► Affected Male
   Circle       ──► Normal Female             Filled Circle  ──► Affected Female
   Diamond      ──► Sex Unspecified           Filled Diamond ──► Affected Unspecified
   Single Line  ──► Mating                    Double Line    ──► Consanguineous Mating (Relatives)
conceptBreakdown.content:
### 9.1 Standard Pedigree Symbols
- **Square**: Normal male; **Circle**: Normal female; **Diamond**: Sex unspecified.
- **Filled/Solid Symbols**: Affected individuals expressing the phenotype.
- **Single Horizontal Line**: Mating; **Double Horizontal Line**: Consanguineous mating (mating between biological relatives).
- **Roman Numerals (I, II, III)**: Successive generations; **Arabic Numerals (1, 2, 3)**: Individuals within a generation.

### 9.2 Pedigree Pattern Recognition Algorithms

```
                     PEDIGREE PATTERN RECOGNITION RULES
                     
   1. AUTOSOMAL DOMINANT (e.g., Myotonic Dystrophy, Huntington's):
      ├── Does NOT skip generations; affected child MUST have affected parent.
      └── Both males and females affected with equal frequency.
      
   2. AUTOSOMAL RECESSIVE (e.g., Sickle-Cell, PKU, Thalassemia):
      ├── Skips generations; affected child can have unaffected carrier parents (Aa x Aa).
      └── Consanguineous mating increases incidence.
      
   3. X-LINKED RECESSIVE (e.g., Hemophilia, Color Blindness):
      ├── Preponderance of affected MALES (X^d Y).
      └── Criss-cross inheritance: Affected mother (X^d X^d) passes to ALL sons (X^d Y).
          Affected father (X^d Y) passes mutant X to ALL daughters (carriers X^d X), NEVER to sons.
```

conceptBreakdown.heading: X-Linked Dominant and Y-Linked Rules
conceptBreakdown.title: X-Linked Dominant and Y-Linked Rules
conceptBreakdown.content: In X-Linked Dominant pedigrees (e.g. Hypophosphatemic Rickets), an affected male passes the trait to ALL daughters and NO sons. In Y-linked (Holandric) traits (e.g. Hypertrichosis of pinna), affected fathers transmit the trait strictly to ALL sons.

conceptBreakdown.heading: Mitochondrial (Maternal) Inheritance Patterns
conceptBreakdown.title: Mitochondrial (Maternal) Inheritance Patterns
conceptBreakdown.content: Mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) is transmitted strictly through the egg cytoplasm; an affected mother transmits the condition (e.g. Leber's Hereditary Optic Neuropathy) to 100% of her children (both sons and daughters), while affected fathers never transmit it.
